[  edit  ]
The Noise  SOP  displaces geometry points using noise patterns. It uses the same math as the  Noise CHOP .

parameters.label: Group
parameters.name: group
parameters.description: If there are input groups, specifying a group name in this field will cause this  SOP  to act only upon the group specified. Accepts patterns, as described in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu sets which attribute of the geometry the Noise  SOP  acts on.

parameters.label: Point Position
parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Noise is applied in the direction of the point normal. If no normal is specified, a normal is computed.

parameters.label: Point Normals
parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Noise is applied to each component of the normal independently and then the vector is renormalized.

parameters.label: Point Diffuse Color
parameters.name: cd
parameters.description: Noise is applied to each component of the color independently.

parameters.label: Point Alpha
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Noise is applied to alpha.

parameters.label: Point Texture UV
parameters.name: uv
parameters.description: Noise is applied to each component uv independently.

parameters.label: Point Texture W
parameters.name: w
parameters.description: Noise is applied to texture w.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - The noise function used to generate noise. The functions available are:

parameters.label: Sparse
parameters.name: sparse
parameters.description: Produces high quality, continuous noise based on Sparse Convolution.

parameters.label: Hermite
parameters.name: hermite
parameters.description: Quicker than Sparse, but produces lower quality noise.

parameters.label: Harmomic Summation
parameters.name: harmonic
parameters.description: Sparse noise with the ability to control the frequency step of the harmonics. Takes the longest to compute.

parameters.label: Brownian
parameters.name: brownian
parameters.description: Works like a bug in random flight. With Num of Integrals at 2, its acceleration is changed randomly every frame.

parameters.label: Random
parameters.name: random
parameters.description: (White Noise) Every sample is random and unrelated to any other sample. It is the same as "white noise" in audio.

parameters.label: Alligator
parameters.name: alligator
parameters.description: Cell Noise.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Any number, integer or non-integer, which starts the random number generator. Each number gives completely different noise patterns, but with similar characteristics.

parameters.label: Period
parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The approximate separation between peaks of a noise cycle. It is expressed in Units. Increasing the period stretches the noise pattern out.

parameters.label: Harmonics
parameters.name: harmon
parameters.description: The number of higher frequency components to layer on top of the base frequency. The higher this number, the bumpier the noise will be (as long as roughness is not set to zero). 0 Harmonics give the base shape.

parameters.label: Harmonic Spread
parameters.name: spread
parameters.description: The factor by which the frequency of the harmonics are increased. It is normally 2. A spread of 3 and a base frequency of 0.1Hz will produce harmonics at 0.3Hz, 0.9Hz, 2.7Hz, etc.. This parameter is only valid for the Harmonic Summation type.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.name: rough
parameters.description: Controls the effect of the higher frequency noise. When Roughness is zero, all harmonics above the base frequency have no effect. At one, all harmonics are equal in amplitude to the base frequency. When Roughness is between one and zero, the amplitude of higher harmonics drops off exponentially from the base frequency.

parameters.label: The default roughness is 0.5. This means the amplitude of the first harmonic is 0.5 of the base frequency, the second is 0.25, the third is 0.125. The harmonics are added to the base to give the final shape. The Harmonics parameter and the Roughness parameter must both be non
parameters.description: zero to see the harmonic effects.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.name: exp
parameters.description: Pushes the noise values toward 0, or +1 and -1. (It raises the value to the power of the exponent.) Exponents greater than one will pull the channel toward zero, and powers less than one will pull peaks towards +1 and -1. It is used to reshape the channels.

parameters.label: Number of Integrals
parameters.name: numint
parameters.description: Defines the number of times to integrate (see the  Speed CHOP ) the Brownian noise. Higher values produce smoother curves with fewer features. Values beyond 4 produce somewhat identical curves. This parameter is only valid for the Random noise type.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.name: amp
parameters.description: Defines the noise value's amplitude (a scale on the values output).

parameters.label: The Translate, Rotate, Scale and Pivot parameters let you sample in a different part of the 3D noise space. Imagine a different noise value for every XYZ point in space. Normally, the Noise  SOP  samples the noise space from (0,0,0) along the X
parameters.description: axis in steps of 2/period.

parameters.label: By changing the transform, you are translating, rotating and scaling the line along which the Noise SOPs samples the noise space. A slight Y
parameters.description: rotation is like walking in a straight path in the mountains, recording your altitude along the way, then re-starting from the same initial location, walking in a slightly different direction. Your altitude starts off being similar but then diverges.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - The menu attached to this parameter allows you to specify the order in which the transforms will take place. Changing the Transform order will change where things go much the same way as going a block and turning east gets you to a different place than turning east and then going a block.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - The rotational matrix presented when you click on this option allows you to set the transform order for the rotations. As with transform order (above), changing the order in which the rotations take place will alter the final position.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - Translate the sampling plane through the noise space.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - Rotate the sampling plane in the noise space.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - Scale the sampling plane.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - Control the pivot for the transform of the sampling plane.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.
